data.body:
CLOSE GATE CAUGHT A file_impact MISMATCH, and it was wrong in BOTH directions - the most instructive instance of this pattern in the run so far.

The close refused because commit c1b1402a77 changes src/rebar/llm/code_review/repeat_fix.py, undeclared. That file is the story's OWN NEW OWNER MODULE - the whole point of the change - so the record omitted the single most important path.

Comparing the recorded file_impact against what the landed commits actually touched:
  DECLARED BUT NEVER TOUCHED (3): src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py, tests/unit/llm/code_review/test_bugfix_size_gate.py, tests/unit/plan_review/test_bug_escalation.py. The last two are not real paths in this tree at all - the actual suites are tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py and tests/unit/test_bugfix_repeat_fix_1dd5.py.
  TOUCHED BUT NOT DECLARED (3): repeat_fix.py, tests/unit/test_bugfix_repeat_fix_1dd5.py, tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py.

So the declaration was written from the plan's GUESSED paths and never reconciled against the implementation. It is now set to the six files the work actually touched, each with the reason it was touched.

Running tally of this failure mode in this epic: 1cf6 (Scope named gc_trigger.py, file_impact omitted it), 7931 (Scope named bridge.py after review remediation, file_impact never updated), a73e (I declared only the test file before implementation revealed a source marker was needed), d6e3 (push_recovery.py omitted), and now 1dd5 (guessed paths, wrong in both directions). Five of them. Nothing reconciles Scope, file_impact and the actual diff until the close gate does - which is late, but it has caught every single one.
